previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease and newly diagnosed high-grade osteosarcoma of the left tibia was admitted for her first cycle of adjuvant chemotherapy with doxorubicin and cisplatin. She had recently undergone tumor resection and was recovering at home with ongoing narcotic pain management. A port was successfully placed on admission for chemotherapy access. She tolerated the treatment well, with only transient mild chest pressure that resolved spontaneously and normal cardiac workup. Her anemia, related to chronic hemolysis from sickle cell disease, was managed with a single unit of packed red blood cells prior to discharge. She remained stable throughout the hospitalization, received pegfilgrastim (Neulasta) to support white blood cell recovery, and was discharged home with clear instructions on infection prevention, medication management, and follow-up for subsequent chemotherapy cycles.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ woman with neutropenia and now cough.  Question
pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  ___.

PA AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  While there is again mild interstitial
prominence, the opacities in the right lower lobe appear to be slightly worse
than on several comparison films.  A right-sided Port-A-Cath terminates in the
right atrium.  Left lung appears with chronic interstitial markings but no
evidence of pneumonia.  No pleural effusion or pneumothorax is seen.

IMPRESSION:  More so than on past exams, prominence of the right lower lobe
interstitial markings could be consistent with an early or atypical pneumonia
in this neutropenic patient.

INDICATION:  Sickle cell, hepatitis C, and transaminitis after chemotherapy. 
Evaluate for cirrhosis or acute process.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal ultrasound ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Abdominal ultrasound.

FINDINGS:  The liver is normal in echogenicity and echotexture without focal
liver lesions are seen.  Doppler assessment of the main portal vein
demonstrates patency and hepatopetal flow.  There is no ascites in the
abdomen.  The gallbladder has been surgically removed.  The common bile duct
is not dilated measuring 3 mm.  The right kidney measures 10.2 cm without
hydronephrosis or stones.  The left kidney is obscured by overlying bowel gas
and cannot be fully evaluated.  The body of the pancreas is unremarkable,
however the head and tail are obscured by overlying bowel gas.  The spleen has
been surgically removed.  The aorta is of normal caliber throughout.  The
visualized portions of the inferior vena cava appear normal.

IMPRESSION:  Normal abdominal ultrasound.  Cirrhosis cannot be excluded by
ultrasound.

microbiology.comments: NEGATIVE FOR CMV IgM ANTIBODY BY EIA.  INTERPRETATION:  INFECTION AT UNDETERMINED TIME.  A positive IgG result generally indicates past exposure.  Infection with CMV once contracted remains latent and may reactivate when immunity is compromised.  If current infection is suspected, submit follow-up serum in 2-3 weeks.  Greatly elevated serum protein with IgG levels >2000 mg/dl may cause  interference with CMV IgM results.

NEGATIVE <1:10 BY IFA.  INTERPRETATION: RESULTS INDICATIVE OF PAST EBV INFECTION.  In most populations, 90% of adults have been infected at sometime with EBV and will have measurable VCA IgG and EBNA antibodies. Antibodies to EBNA develop 6-8 weeks after primary infection and remain present for life. Presence of VCA IgM antibodies indicates recent primary infection.
CMV DNA not detected.  Performed by PCR.  Detection Range: 600 - 100,000 copies/ml.
